That script is NOT in this repo and must not be vendored here -- it ships with the pm-skills plugin, enabled at project scope in .claude/settings.json. Resolve it, do not hardcode: PM_SCRIPTS=$(find ~/.claude/plugins -path '*/pm-skills/scripts' -type d -print -quit) then python3 "$PM_SCRIPTS/delivery_loop_gate.py" --plan specs/sprint-2-loop-plan.json --mode plan --output human. See charter section 9. Every task carries acceptance.cmd rather than acceptance.criterion -- with a single human, owner == reviewer, and machine verification is what makes that non-circular (charter section 4).

closed.gate: bash -c 'set -e; EXPECT=34c869f227c1a62145342f0212645a8f898160f6b4589e3cec0e9baad74c692d; mapfile -t G < <(find ~/.claude/plugins -path "*/pm-skills/scripts/delivery_loop_gate.py" | sort); [ ${#G[@]} -ge 1 ] || { echo "FAIL: no delivery_loop_gate.py found"; exit 1; }; H=$(printf "%s\n" "${G[@]}" | xargs sha256sum | awk "{print \$1}" | sort -u); [ "$(printf "%s\n" "$H" | wc -l)" = 1 ] || { echo "FAIL: installs differ -- pin one"; exit 1; }; [ "$H" = "$EXPECT" ] || { echo "FAIL: gate is $H but the archived verdict came from $EXPECT -- re-verify and update gate and gate_sha256 together"; exit 1; }; python3 "${G[0]}" --plan specs/sprint-2-loop-plan.json --mode close --output human'
closed.gate_note: This field was 'delivery_loop_gate.py --mode close' -- a bare script name presented as reproducible evidence for a gate that is not vendored in this repo, so it would not run from a fresh checkout. PLZG-129, a recurrence of PLZG-117, which was the same defect in charter prose. It is now written resolved and re-runnable. It deliberately does NOT use 'find -print -quit', the form this file's own $comment still recommends: that resolver is non-deterministic run to run, 5/10 each way over ten runs, recorded in sprint-3-loop-plan.json's T6 evidence and still open as PLZG-118 defect 2. Instead the resolver enumerates every match, sorts, fails on zero, and fails on two or more that are not byte-identical, so only an unambiguous resolution runs. The $comment's -quit guidance is left alone as PLZG-118's to fix; changing it here would make this a two-concern change.
closed.gate_sha256: 34c869f227c1a62145342f0212645a8f898160f6b4589e3cec0e9baad74c692d -- the delivery_loop_gate.py that returned CLOSE-OK for this plan on 2026-08-09. The gate command ASSERTS this value and exits 1 if the resolved gate differs, so it cannot silently re-derive the archived verdict with a different binary. Recorded and checked, not recorded and trusted: an earlier revision stored the hash while the command only checked the two installs agreed with each other, which a reviewer correctly called out as a value nothing verified. If a plugin upgrade makes this fail, that is the design -- re-run, confirm the verdict, and update both fields in one change.
closed.reverified_at: 2026-08-09 -- verdict re-obtained by executing the gate string above verbatim, rather than trusting the 2026-07-30 record. CLOSE-OK, exit 0, 10 of 10 tasks done. The original verdict stands; what changed is that it can now be re-derived from this file.
closed.note: Every task carries acceptance.cmd rather than acceptance.criterion, so owner == reviewer stays non-circular: adam reviewing adam's prose is self-attestation, adam reviewing an exit code is not (charter section 4).
